questions.question: How does useContext avoid prop drilling? Show an example.
questions.title: useContext in React — Avoiding Prop Drilling with Context API
questions.direct_answer:
How does useContext avoid prop drilling? Show an example.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Provider/Consumer pair; useContext hook; default value; common use for theming, auth, i18n.

**Classic weak answer:** Using a single large Context for everything — any update re-renders every consumer; split Contexts by change frequency.

**Senior finish:** Show a ThemeContext example, and mention context-selector patterns (e.g., use-context-selector) for perf.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **useContext in React — Avoiding Prop Drilling with Context API** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** How does useContext avoid prop drilling? Show an example.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Provider/Consumer pair; useContext hook; default value; common use for theming, auth, i18n**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Using a single large Context for everything — any update re-renders every consumer; split Contexts by change frequency**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Show a ThemeContext example, and mention context-selector patterns (e.g., use-context-selector) for perf**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Provider/Consumer pair; useContext hook; default value; common use for theming, auth, i18n
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

questions.question: When should you use useReducer instead of useState?
questions.title: useReducer vs useState in React — When to Use Each
questions.direct_answer:
When should you use useReducer instead of useState?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** useReducer for complex state transitions, multiple related values, action-based logic; useState for simple values.

**Classic weak answer:** Reaching for Redux immediately — useReducer + Context can replace Redux for many mid-size apps.

**Senior finish:** Show a form with useReducer and a discriminated action union; mention Redux Toolkit's createSlice is a useReducer-flavored API.

questions.question: What are the performance pitfalls of the React Context API?
questions.title: React Context Performance Pitfalls — Re-renders & Fixes
questions.direct_answer:
What are the performance pitfalls of the React Context API?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Every Provider value change re-renders all consumers; unstable object literals; splitting Contexts or using selector libraries.

**Classic weak answer:** Passing a fresh object literal as the Context value every render — unstable reference = cascading re-renders.

**Senior finish:** Show three fixes: useMemo the value, split Contexts by responsibility, or use use-context-selector / Zustand for selector-level subscription.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Passing a fresh object literal as the Context value every render — unstable reference = cascading re-renders
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Show three fixes: useMemo the value, split Contexts by responsibility, or use use-context-selector / Zustand for selector-level subscription
